summaries.backend-sde-nodejs-ts: Backend Software Development Engineer with 3.5+ years of experience and expertise in Node.js, TypeScript, RESTful APIs, and backend system design. Led the AWS SDK for JavaScript v2 to v3 migration across 180+ call sites and 11+ AWS services in production Node.js Lambdas at Turbot HQ, cutting policy-code duplication ~60% while keeping the platform supported past AWS SDK v2 end-of-life.

work.name: Turbot HQ, Inc.
highlights: Led the AWS SDK for JavaScript v2 to v3 migration across 180+ call sites and 11+ AWS services (SecurityHub, CloudWatch, ControlTower, Shield, Comprehend, Pinpoint, RAM, X-Ray, EC2, EFS) in production Node.js Lambdas, refactoring discovery, configuration-sync, tagging, and resource-cleanup workflows; reduced policy-code duplication ~60% via templating and shrank bundle size through modular imports, keeping the platform supported past AWS SDK v2 EOL and unblocking the Node.js runtime upgrade.

Designed and developed a REST API microservice using the Gin framework as part of a greenfield build of Turbot Guardrails, a Preventive Security Posture Management (PSPM) SaaS product; secured endpoints with OAuth 2.0 authentication via Auth0, containerized with Docker, deployed to AWS EC2, and served as a gRPC client for several internal microservices.

Core contributor across four open-source platform-engineering products (Steampipe, Powerpipe, Flowpipe, Tailpipe) — 120+ merged pull requests and 9,300+ GitHub stars — including engineering core throughput and memory optimizations for Tailpipe, lifting log-processing throughput 30% to 1,000+ logs per second via chunked, batched file reads and streaming writes, and eliminating out-of-memory failures.

Optimized complex PostgreSQL queries powering customer compliance audits — rewriting IAM policy-evaluation queries with jsonb array elements and multi-stage CTEs — improving query performance 40% (cutting report generation from 3 minutes to 1.5 minutes across 10,000+ resources) and eliminating a class of false-positive findings.

Built a Kafka-based, event-driven pipeline where consumers asynchronously processed policy-enforcement events and fired a webhook once a policy was successfully enforced against a resource; added a dead-letter queue (DLQ) to capture recurring failures for debugging, and unified GitHub Actions CI/CD release workflows across four production services.
